source_text:
Ἐν ἓξ γὰρ ἡμέραις σύμπας ὁ

αἰσθητὸς συμπεπλήρωται κόσμος· ἐν δὲ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ κατέπαυσεν ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ πάντων
τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ· καὶ οὐκέτι πρόοδος ἄλλου κόσμου καὶ ἔτι προσδοκᾶται πάμπαν
συντελεσθῆναι, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ παρόντος αἰῶνος συντέλειαν· κατὰ δὲ τὸ κατὰ μέρος,
ἕτι μὲν ἐνεργεῖται καθὰ εἴρηται τῷ Σωτῆρι· "ὁ Πατήρ μου ἕως ἄρτι ἐργάζεται, κἀγὼ
ἐργάζομαι·" πεπαύσεται δὲ πάντως καὶ ἡ κατὰ τὴν κοινὴν συντέλειαν· καὶ ἄλλη
τηνικαῦτα πρόοδος ἔσται, καθ' ἣν ἔσται ὁ Θεὸς τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι· καὶ πάντα πρὸς
αὐτὸν ἐπιστρέψουσιν, ἡ τῶν ὅλων μεταστοιχείωσις, καὶ ἐκ φθορᾶς εἰς ἀφθαρσίαν
μεταποίησις.
thought_title: The completed sensible world and the final procession
orientation: Procopius is distinguishing the already-completed universal procession of the generated world from the particular works that continue until the common consummation.
pass_a_gloss: For in six days the whole sensible world has been completed; and on the seventh God rested from all his works; and no longer is a procession of another world even still expected to be completed at all, according to the consummation of the present age; but according to the particular, it is still being worked, as was said by the Savior: "My Father until now is working, and I am working"; and it will cease altogether also at the common consummation; and another procession will be then, according to which God will be all things in all; and all things will return to him, the transformation of all things, and the change from corruption to incorruption.

choices.why: Perfect tense indicates a finished state; 'completed' matches the glossary sense of the universal procession being finished.
Standard biblical language for God's rest on the seventh day (Genesis 2:2); 'rested' is the plain sense.
Fixed glossary term; the central concept being distinguished.
Refers to the end of the age; 'consummation' is the standard theological term and matches the brief's usage.
Fixed glossary term for the final change of all things.
Parallel to transformation; 'change' keeps the literal sense of a making-over from one state to another.

bible_refs.note: ὁ Πατήρ μου ἕως ἄρτι ἐργάζεται, κἀγὼ ἐργάζομαι
ἐν δὲ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ κατέπαυσεν ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ
ἔσται ὁ Θεὸς τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι

pass_b_english: For in six days the whole sensible world was completed, and on the seventh day God rested from all His works. And no longer is any procession of another world still expected to be completed at all, at the consummation of the present age. In its particular aspect, however, it is still being worked, as was said by the Savior: "My Father is working until now, and I am working" (John 5:17). Yet this too will certainly cease at the common consummation. Then there will be another procession, in which God will be all in all (1 Corinthians 15:28), and all things will return to Him—the transformation of all things, and the change from corruption to incorruption.

problems.quote: No procession of another world is expected any longer
problems.source_quote: καὶ οὐκέτι πρόοδος ἄλλου κόσμου καὶ ἔτι προσδοκᾶται πάμπαν συντελεσθῆναι
problems.why: English says 'no longer expected' but Greek says 'no other world procession is still expected to be completed at all'—the καὶ ἔτι ('and still') belongs with προσδοκᾶται, making 'is still expected.' The 'no longer' misreads οὐκέτι position.
problems.fix: And no procession of another world is still expected to be completed at all

problems.quote: until all things are brought to their consummation
problems.source_quote: κατὰ τὴν τοῦ παρόντος αἰῶνος συντέλειαν
problems.why: Greek gives a temporal endpoint ('at the consummation'), not a 'until' clause. English changes when this happens from a fixed point to a duration.
problems.fix: at the consummation of the present age
problems.ruling: Source says 'at the consummation of the present age' (κατὰ τὴν...συντέλειαν), a point in time; 'until' wrongly makes it a duration.

edits.old: No procession of another world is expected any longer, until all things are brought to their consummation at the end of the present age.
edits.new: And no procession of another world is still expected to be completed at all, at the consummation of the present age.

problems.quote: And no procession of another world is still expected to be completed at all
problems.source_quote: καὶ οὐκέτι πρόοδος ἄλλου κόσμου καὶ ἔτι προσδοκᾶται πάμπαν συντελεσθῆναι
problems.why: Greek says 'no longer...is still expected' (οὐκέτι...καὶ ἔτι), English omits 'no longer', flipping to 'no...is still expected'.
problems.fix: And no longer is any procession of another world still expected to be completed at all
problems.ruling: οὐκέτι means 'no longer'; English 'no...is still expected' loses the 'no longer' sense, slightly altering meaning.

edits.old: And no procession of another world is still expected to be completed at all, at the consummation of the present age.
edits.new: And no longer is any procession of another world still expected to be completed at all, at the consummation of the present age.

fixed: Changed 'And no procession' to 'And no longer is any procession' to restore the Greek 'οὐκέτι' (no longer) that was omitted.

problems.quote: as was said by the Savior
problems.why: Scripture quote introduced without clear marker; could be author or Jesus.
Ambiguous: shared end of all things, or ordinary completion?
problems.fix: Use 'universal consummation' or 'shared end of all things'.

problems.quote: projection of the one and only Holy Spirit
problems.why: 'Projection' in heading and 'procession' in body seem to refer to the same concept but use different words.
problems.fix: Use 'procession' consistently, or explain 'projection' as a synonym.

edits.old: as was said by the Savior:

fixed: The glossary issue about 'projection' does not appear in the provided English or literal gloss; the English consistently uses 'procession', so no change is needed.

problems.why: Clear attribution; but 'My Father is working until now' functions as prooftext whose interpretation is disputed—reader may not grasp author uses it against eternal creation.
problems.fix: Note author reads this as limited temporal work.

problems.quote: God will be all in all (1 Corinthians 15:28)
problems.why: Citation is correct but author's application as 'another procession' is theological interpretation, not literal quotation; however, 'the transformation of all things' may allude to 2 Peter 3:13 or Romans 8:21 without citation.
problems.fix: Note author's interpretive application of 1 Cor 15:28.

edits.new: as was said by the Savior:

edits.old: God will be all in all (1 Corinthians 15:28), and all things will return to Him—the transformation of all things, and the change from corruption to incorruption.
edits.new: God will be all in all (1 Corinthians 15:28), and all things will return to Him—the transformation of all things, and the change from corruption to incorruption.

fixed: The speaker attribution 'as Jesus says in John' was changed back to 'as was said by the Savior' to match the source's introduction by the Savior, not by the author's own naming of Jesus in John.
The scripture citation for 1 Corinthians 15:28 is correct and the author's application as 'another procession' is already clear from the surrounding text; no change needed.
